operations.evidence: Pre-April-2013 detection-regime boundary was preserved.
Detection-era categories were not treated as current outcomes or parcel scores.
Broader outcomes supply from April 2014 and provisional publication history were recorded.
April 2014 was retained as a framework boundary, not an incident-date boundary.
The framework principle that no outcome is favoured and appropriateness is central was recorded.
Outcome numbers were not ranked as a performance or safety ladder.
The victim-oriented purpose and removal of detection-target incentives were recorded.
Policy purpose was not treated as evidence of individual victim experience.
Transparency, accountability and community-engagement purposes were recorded.
Accountability information was not converted to parcel risk.
Recorded-offence and charged-offence distinction under CPS standards was preserved.
Alternative offence was not treated as a recording error or replacement of the original offence.
Outcome 1A alternative charge-or-summons semantics were recorded.
Outcome 1A was not merged with outcome 1 or treated as conviction.
Outcome 2A alternative youth-caution semantics were recorded.
Outcome 2A was not merged with outcome 2 without explicit grouping.
Outcome 3A alternative adult-caution semantics were recorded.
Outcome 3A was kept edition-aware and non-ordinal.
Voluntary April 2016 and mandatory April 2017 transition dates were recorded.
Pre-adoption absence was not treated as absence of alternative-offence disposals.
Recorded-period linked cohort tracing and maturation were recorded.
Young cohorts were not treated as complete.
Sexual-offence outcome lag and later cohort maturation were recorded.
Same-year resolution was not treated as mature resolution.
Closed-investigation volumes were preserved as an activity view independent of offence-recording year.
Closed-period volumes were not substituted for a linked cohort.
The possibility of illustrative closed-period rates exceeding 100 percent was recorded.
Rates over 100 percent were not automatically classified as errors.
Timeliness was recorded as a qualified proxy rather than a firm efficiency measure.
Administrative delay and case mix remained explicit.
Outcome action and system-entry dates were preserved as potentially different.
Recorded duration was not represented as pure investigation time.
The cannabis-warning same-day action versus later system entry example was recorded.
The example was not generalized to every outcome.
Transferred-or-cancelled scope and reason families were recorded.
Transfer/cancellation was not equated with acquittal or false reporting.

The data were not used to measure all decisions not to record.
Financial-year assignment of transfer/cancellation events was recorded.
Process-event counts were not treated as original-offence cohorts.
Outside-jurisdiction transfer semantics were recorded.
Transfer was not interpreted as no crime.

The reason was kept separate from duplication and recording error.

Duplicate cancellation was not treated as invalidating the underlying event.
Recorded-in-error cancellation was preserved as a distinct reason.
The category was not generalized to force-wide accuracy.
Specified-assault self-defence cancellation was recorded.
The category was not inferred outside its documented offence scope.
